Subject: Post-demo: BorealX deployment guardrails & routing policy next steps

Hi Tim / Sanjay — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can keep momentum on the pilot. TL;DR: BorealX wants predictable latency for search/rerank and cost controls for high-volume calls; we recommended a mixed routing policy + canary fallback chain and a private VPC peering plan for data isolation.

Recap of key technical asks (from the call):
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 150ms for query -> reranker path.
- Cost target: keep avg token cost below $0.0009/token for gen + reranker ops.
- Embeddings store: ~12M vectors (768 dim) initial, expect 3x growth in 6 months.
- Auth: customer-managed API keys + optional mTLS for private deployment.
- Region: primary us-west; GD/DR routing to eu-west when us capacity saturates.
- Fallbacks: prefer hosted full-precision model; fallback to quantized private node with warmed KV cache for cold starts.

Open items / asks for your team before we spin up pilot:
1) Confirm VPC peering CIDR blocks or allowlist IPs for outbound egress to Redwood dedicated endpoints.
2) Share an example prompt set we should use for reranker/eval (5–10 queries covering worst-case latency).
3) Procurement: who should I loop in for the SOW and PO timeline (I copied procurement@borealx.com if different please advise).
4) Security review owners: if you can share the primary contact for the SOC2/data retention questions, we’ll send the packet.

What we'll deliver this week (Redwood):
- Draft SOW + pricing band (attached: borealx-sow-draft.docx).
- Deployment guardrails doc with proposed routing policy (attached: redwood-deployment-guardrails-v1.pdf).
- Sample SDK snippet + auth examples for quick smoke tests (attached: sample-sdk-snippet.py).

Suggested immediate next steps:
- Tim: confirm network allowlist and procurement contact by EOD Wednesday (11/11).
- BorealX: send a small reranker prompt set by Fri (11/13).
- Redwood: Camila will schedule a 30-minute SDK setup session early next week to walk through auth and structured output/tool-calling patterns.

I’ll follow up with a technical plan that maps routing policy -> model variants -> canary percentages and fallback timing, but wanted to get these asks on your radar.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0129

Subject: Tech follow-up: SDK auth snippet + proposed routing policy (for BorealX)

Camila / Neha — following Tim's ask, here's what I recommend we bring to the SDK session next week and what to include in the pilot config. Please review and flag anything missing before I send to BorealX.

Proposed pilot config (summary):
- Models: primary hosted model (gpt-redwood-14b), fallback private quantized node (rw-q8) for cost-sensitive flows.
- Canary: start with 10% traffic to rw-q8 for reranker calls for 2 weeks; monitor quality/regressions against the eval set.
- Fallback chain: hosted full-precision -> rw-q8 private -> stubbed cached response (for extreme degradation). Auto-fallback on p95 latency > 300ms or 5% error rate.
- Routing policy: region-based (us-west primary), cost-cap throttle per minute (configurable), and per-route latency SLOs.
- Embeddings: index in Redwood-Managed vector store with replication in eu-west for DR. Estimated storage + egress cost included in SOW.

SDK auth example (attached sample-sdk-snippet.py) — include both API-key header and mTLS note in session. We'll demo:
- quick token-based smoke test (no firewall changes)
- VPC-only mTLS flow (requires allowlist + cert exchange)

Planned deliverables this week: 1) finalize the SOW (I will update pricing bands to reflect canary), 2) provide a routing policy JSON template and a short-runbook for canary rollback, 3) schedule SDK setup session (Camila — can you take Wed or Thu next week?).

Also attaching a short checklist for the SDK session:
- Confirm API key issuance and rotation policy.
- Show structured output + tool-calling example for reranker/QA path.
- Walk through embeddings ingestion (batch vs streaming).

Ben

Attachments: sample-sdk-snippet.py (py, 3KB), redwood-deployment-guardrails-v1.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)
